The solution is y≤0 together with the entire y-axis. Option 1 includes these solid boundaries and matches the worked diagram.\nq-121262: -x²y²≤0 everywhere, so the whole plane is shaded. Option 3 matches the worked diagram.\nq-6880: The semiaxes are 4 horizontally and 2 vertically, giving x=4cos(θ), y=2sin(θ).\nq-79281: x=2cos(θ), y=4sin(θ) starts at (2,0) with upward velocity, traversing the ellipse counterclockwise once.\nq-106706: Center (-3,2) and semiaxes 6 and 4 give x=6cos(θ)-3, y=4sin(θ)+2, as stated in its own solution.\nq-78682: Both coordinates are nonnegative on [0,π/2], producing exactly the pictured first-quadrant arc, including its endpoints.\nq-15843: Squaring x/6=cos(θ) and y/2=sin(θ), then adding, gives x²/36+y²/4=1.\nq-106408: Squaring 2(x-2)=cos(θ) and 2(y-3)=sin(θ), then adding, gives 4(x-2)²+4(y-3)²=1.\nq-75992: -(x+5)(x-3)>0 between its roots, excluding them: -5<x<3.\nq-142180: -(x-3)(x-6)≥0 between its roots, including them: 3≤x≤6.\nq-70303: -(x+3)(x-1)<0 outside its roots: x<-3 or x>1.\nq-142315: -(x-1)(x-5)≤0 outside its roots, including them: x≤1 or x≥5.\nq-3881: x(4-x)≥0 gives [0,4].\nq-3951: (2x-3)(x+4)≤0 gives [-4,3/2].\n\nThe source's central-angle error does not change any final answer, so every answer's disagrees flag is false.
